Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. {"arxiv_id":"2611.08364","authors":["Chang Shi","Ann Majewicz Fey"],"categories":["cs.RO","cs.LG"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08364"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T17:42:31Z","rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. Existing methods use geometric rules or hard stability masks, limiting how risk can influence the joint choice of box, orientation, and placement. We propose Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability. A 3D U-Net learns stability from executed outcomes and simulated alternatives, revealing outcomes of actions underrepresented in early rollouts. A discrete on-policy actor--critic uses stability predictions in both its action values and policy prior, with gates that limit the effect of an untrained or changing model. In deployment, SHORE does not require additional search or simulation overhead. In Isaac Gym, SHORE reaches 73\\% space utilization by 0.4M environment steps, while the same learner without stability modeling reaches that level at about 1M. On the expanded 60-box set, SHORE achieves 0.734 space utilization versus 0.588 for the GOPT state-of-the-art baseline, with a higher placement-failure frequency (1.03\\% vs. 0.63\\%), trading more risk for greater packed volume. Ablations suggest that simulated alternatives provide useful early supervision, while executed outcomes alone sustain later performance. We also demonstrate the method on a real robot to verify the simplicity of integrating the method to real bin packing pipelines.","title":"SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing","title_en":"SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08364v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T17:42:31Z"}

## ⚠️ Breaking changes (v0.6.1 -> v0.7.0)

v0.7.0 rebuilds installation, training, inference and the hardware layer. A few changes need your attention when upgrading:

**Installation**
- On Linux, `torch` and `torchvision` now come from PyPI as CUDA 13 builds (NVIDIA driver 580.65 or newer); the `cu128` index is gone. For older drivers, install torch from a CUDA 12 index first (see the installation guide). macOS needs 14+ (15+ for MPS).
- Pins moved: `transformers` 5.22, `huggingface-hub>=1.31, < 3`, `motorbridge` 0.5, `datasets < 6`, `Pillow < 14`, `torchcodec < 0.18`.

**Training**
- Weights & Biases is replaced by Trackio (the `training` extra installs `trackio`): `--wandb.*` is now `--trackio.*`, `entity`/`mode` have no equivalent, remote jobs with tracking need `--trackio.space_id`, and checkpoints are no longer uploaded as artifacts by default.
- FSDP1 is replaced by FSDP2/HSDP (`--parallelism.dp_shard`, `--parallelism.dp_replicate`, `--accelerator.*`); mixed precision is set with `--accelerator.mixed_precision`. FSDP checkpoints saved with lerobot ≤ 0.6.x cannot be resumed (their `model.safetensors` still loads), and Accelerate YAML/env configuration is rejected unless `LEROBOT_ALLOW_ACCELERATE_ENV=1`.
- `--policy.use_peft=true` alone now trains LoRA instead of silently fully fine-tuning.
- Image transforms are batched: `GaussianNoise`, `MotionBlur`, `GaussianPatchBrightness`, `RandomShadow`, `CoarseDropout`, `GammaCorrection` and `PlanckianJitter` were silent no-ops on uint8 frames and now apply. `ImageTransforms` takes tensors only; the per-sample classes are deprecated.

**Inference & rollout**
- `lerobot.async_inference` and `lerobot[async]` are removed: use `lerobot[remote]`, `lerobot-policy-server` and `lerobot-rollout --inference.type=remote`. `lerobot.rollout.inference` moved to `lerobot.inference`.
- `select_action` / `predict_action_chunk` may return a `PolicyOutput` (`{"action", "prediction"}`) instead of a bare tensor; use `policy_output_to_transition` when calling them directly.
- With `--interpolation_multiplier>1`, rollout strategies record one frame per policy action instead of one per tick.

**Simulation & environments**
- `lerobot.envs. ` moved to `lerobot.sim.integrations. `, env configs are named `*EnvConfig` (`LiberoEnv` -> `LiberoEnvConfig`), and in-process envs return canonical observations (HWC uint8 images, flat float32 state; map camera names with `--rename_map`). `--env.type` is unchanged.
- Removed env fields: Aloha/PushT `observation_height`/`observation_width`, MetaWorld `episode_length`/`multitask_eval`, RoboTwin `obs_type`/`render_mode`. MetaWorld's default task is `metaworld-push-v3`.
- EnvHub `make_env` is called without `cfg` and must return an unwrapped `SyncVectorEnv`/`AsyncVectorEnv` unless `--env.use_native_batch=true`.

**Policies**
- `dtype` is the single precision key of every policy config; `torch_dtype`, `vlm_dtype`, `model_params_fp32` and `model_dtype` are ignored or removed. In Python pass `torch.bfloat16`, not a string.

- EO1: `chunk_size` and `n_action_steps` default to 16.
- VLA-JEPA: checkpoints trained before the RoPE fix need `--policy.world_model_rope_legacy=true`; `binarize_gripper_action` and `pre_snap_gripper_action` default to `false`.

**Datasets**
- `--dataset.streaming=true` uses a new disk-less episode-pool reader with `--dataset.streaming_*` options; `Backtrackable` is removed.

**Hardware**
- Feetech and Dynamixel run on one rustypot-backed `SerialMotorsBus` (`lerobot[feetech]`/`[dynamixel]` install `rustypot` instead of the vendor SDKs). `FeetechMotorsBus`/`DynamixelMotorsBus` are deprecated aliases, `OperatingMode`/`TorqueMode` give way to `bus.set_operating_mode("position")`, and the control tables, `encoding_utils` and the SDK-level helpers (`broadcast_ping`, `scan_port`, ...) are removed. {"arxiv_id":"2611.08462","authors":["Arpit Bahety","Skand Peri","Sriniket Ambatipudi","Chen Xu","Haruki Nishimura","Masha Itkina","Roberto Martín-Martín"],"categories":["cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08462"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["vla"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T18:53:16Z","rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Özaslan","Tolga Özaslan"],"categories":["cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08139"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":[],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T15:03:10Z","rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Frontier-based exploration systems repeatedly evaluate geodesic travel costs between robot poses and candidate viewpoints, and tour-based planners consume the full pairwise distance matrix built from them. Recomputing these matrices with one graph search per source scales with the explored map size, whereas distance caches that refresh only locally affected or newly created frontiers can retain stale costs between surviving pairs when newly discovered free space creates a global shortcut. We present H-TRIP (Hierarchical Tropical Rank-one Incremental Propagation), an exact distance index grounded in Kleene algebra over the min-plus semiring for monotonically growing occupancy grids. H-TRIP partitions the known map into a spatial hierarchy with fixed boundary ports. Each unknown-to-free revelation is decomposed into efficient rank-one min-plus edge insertions at the affected leaf, and only decreased port-to-port summaries are propagated along its ancestor chain. A shared hierarchical lift evaluates the dense many-to-many matrix of shortest distances for all active query points on the occupancy map. We prove that sequential insertions preserve exact shortest-path distances on the grid. Benchmark experiments confirm exact agreement with reference searches on fully built maps and show that dense many-to-many queries at a few dozen viewpoints are up to two orders of magnitude faster than sequential k x BFS. On exploration runs with sixteen robots, in-loop queries on the growing occupancy graph are 2.21x-8.59x faster than co-scheduled k x BFS on maps with side 256, 512, and 1024 cells.","title":"H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration","title_en":"H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08139v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T15:03:10Z"}

Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it.\n  On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer's log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns.\n  Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer's log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.","title":"Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning","title_en":"Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08144v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T15:05:07Z"}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.08373","authors":["Fuhao Li","Wenxuan Song","Qizhou Huang","Ziyang Zhou","Jingbo Wang","Junwu E","Pengwei Wang","Yan Wang","Shunbo Zhou","Haoang Li"],"categories":["cs.RO"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08373"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["vla"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T17:52:16Z","rule_score":90,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.","title":"SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training","title_en":"SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08373v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T17:52:16Z"}

Bhatt","Matthias Scheutz","Ufuk Topcu"],"categories":["cs.RO","cs.AI"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08425"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["vla"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T18:21:07Z","rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success. We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.","title":"Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing","title_en":"Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08425v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T18:21:07Z"}

{"arxiv_id":"2611.08364","authors":["Chang Shi","Ann Majewicz Fey"],"categories":["cs.RO","cs.LG"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08364"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["reinforcement_learning"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T17:42:31Z","rule_score":70,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. Existing methods use geometric rules or hard stability masks, limiting how risk can influence the joint choice of box, orientation, and placement. We propose Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability. A 3D U-Net learns stability from executed outcomes and simulated alternatives, revealing outcomes of actions underrepresented in early rollouts. A discrete on-policy actor--critic uses stability predictions in both its action values and policy prior, with gates that limit the effect of an untrained or changing model. In deployment, SHORE does not require additional search or simulation overhead. In Isaac Gym, SHORE reaches 73\\% space utilization by 0.4M environment steps, while the same learner without stability modeling reaches that level at about 1M. On the expanded 60-box set, SHORE achieves 0.734 space utilization versus 0.588 for the GOPT state-of-the-art baseline, with a higher placement-failure frequency (1.03\\% vs. 0.63\\%), trading more risk for greater packed volume. The results show faster learning and higher utilization on the more demanding realistic box arrival set. ## ⚠️ Breaking changes (v0.6.1 -> v0.7.0)

v0.7.0 rebuilds installation, training, inference and the hardware layer. A few changes need your attention when upgrading:

**Installation**
- On Linux, `torch` and `torchvision` now come from PyPI as CUDA 13 builds (NVIDIA driver 580.65 or newer); the `cu128` index is gone. For older drivers, install torch from a CUDA 12 index first (see the installation guide). macOS needs 14+ (15+ for MPS).
- Pins moved: `transformers` 5.22, `huggingface-hub>=1.31, < 3`, `motorbridge` 0.5, `datasets < 6`, `Pillow < 14`, `torchcodec < 0.18`.

**Training**
- Weights & Biases is replaced by Trackio (the `training` extra installs `trackio`): `--wandb.*` is now `--trackio.*`, `entity`/`mode` have no equivalent, remote jobs with tracking need `--trackio.space_id`, and checkpoints are no longer uploaded as artifacts by default.
- FSDP1 is replaced by FSDP2/HSDP (`--parallelism.dp_shard`, `--parallelism.dp_replicate`, `--accelerator.*`); mixed precision is set with `--accelerator.mixed_precision`. FSDP checkpoints saved with lerobot ≤ 0.6.x cannot be resumed (their `model.safetensors` still loads), and Accelerate YAML/env configuration is rejected unless `LEROBOT_ALLOW_ACCELERATE_ENV=1`.
- `--policy.use_peft=true` alone now trains LoRA instead of silently fully fine-tuning.
- Image transforms are batched: `GaussianNoise`, `MotionBlur`, `GaussianPatchBrightness`, `RandomShadow`, `CoarseDropout`, `GammaCorrection` and `PlanckianJitter` were silent no-ops on uint8 frames and now apply. `ImageTransforms` takes tensors only; the per-sample classes are deprecated.

**Inference & rollout**
- `lerobot.async_inference` and `lerobot[async]` are removed: use `lerobot[remote]`, `lerobot-policy-server` and `lerobot-rollout --inference.type=remote`. `lerobot.rollout.inference` moved to `lerobot.inference`.
- `select_action` / `predict_action_chunk` may return a `PolicyOutput` (`{"action", "prediction"}`) instead of a bare tensor; use `policy_output_to_transition` when calling them directly.
- With `--interpolation_multiplier>1`, rollout strategies record one frame per policy action instead of one per tick.

**Simulation & environments**
- `lerobot.envs. ` moved to `lerobot.sim.integrations. `, env configs are named `*EnvConfig` (`LiberoEnv` -> `LiberoEnvConfig`), and in-process envs return canonical observations (HWC uint8 images, flat float32 state; map camera names with `--rename_map`). `--env.type` is unchanged.
- Removed env fields: Aloha/PushT `observation_height`/`observation_width`, MetaWorld `episode_length`/`multitask_eval`, RoboTwin `obs_type`/`render_mode`. MetaWorld's default task is `metaworld-push-v3`.
- EnvHub `make_env` is called without `cfg` and must return an unwrapped `SyncVectorEnv`/`AsyncVectorEnv` unless `--env.use_native_batch=true`.

**Policies**
- `dtype` is the single precision key of every policy config; `torch_dtype`, `vlm_dtype`, `model_params_fp32` and `model_dtype` are ignored or removed. In Python pass `torch.bfloat16`, not a string.
- MolmoAct2: `enable_lora_vlm`, `enable_lora_action_expert` and `train_action_expert_only` are replaced by `--policy.train_mode_vlm={fft,lora,freeze}`; `action_mode` defaults to `continuous`.
- EO1: `chunk_size` and `n_action_steps` default to 16.
- VLA-JEPA: checkpoints trained before the RoPE fix need `--policy.world_model_rope_legacy=true`; `binarize_gripper_action` and `pre_snap_gripper_action` default to `false`.

**Datasets**
- `--dataset.streaming=true` uses a new disk-less episode-pool reader with `--dataset.streaming_*` options; `Backtrackable` is removed.

**Hardware**
- Feetech and Dynamixel run on one rustypot-backed `SerialMotorsBus` (`lerobot[feetech]`/`[dynamixel]` install `rustypot` instead of the vendor SDKs). `FeetechMotorsBus`/`DynamixelMotorsBus` are deprecated aliases, `OperatingMode`/`TorqueMode` give way to `bus.set_operating_mode("position")`, and the control tables, `encoding_utils` and the SDK-level helpers (`broadcast_ping`, `scan_port`, ...) are removed. Calibration files are unchanged.
- reBot B601: the config is driven by `motor_family` (`dm`, `rs`); `gripper_mit_kp`/`gripper_mit_kd` are removed and per-joint gains take a dict instead of a list.

{"arxiv_id":"2611.08413","authors":["Mohammed Hassan","Zhenyang Chen","Zheng Wang","Zhixin Zhu","Tianlong Chen","Yingyan","Lin","Chaojian Li"],"categories":["cs.RO","cs.CV"],"claims_status":"author_claims_not_independently_reproduced","doi":null,"evidence_scope":"abstract_and_metadata_only","identifiers":{"arxiv":"2611.08413"},"kind":"preprint","method_tags":["vla"],"publication_date_basis":"arxiv_first_submission","published_at":"2026-11-05T18:17:29Z","rule_score":60,"selection_reason":"规则排序（非 AI、非质量评审）：官方来源 +20；有摘要/发行说明 +20；明确版本 +10；每个匹配子领域 +10（最多 +40）。","summary":"Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive. These results demonstrate that training-free token refinement is a practical approach to efficient and robust VLA inference.","title":"T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models","title_en":"T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08413v1","version":"v1","version_updated_at":"2026-11-05T18:17:29Z"}
